introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examinations. 0540 FOOD AND NUTRITION 1, JUNE 2025, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, duration one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination and have an eraser; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the booklet is headed "ORDINARY LEVEL - 0540 FOOD AND NUTRITION 1"; fill in the information required on the booklet and on the answer sheet (Candidate Name, Exam Session, Subject Code and Candidate Identification Number). Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question; to change an answer, erase the first mark carefully, then mark the new answer. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces in the question booklet. At the end of the examination, the invigilator collects the answer sheet first and then the question booklet.
incertitudes: Scan sans couche texte, lu en image page par page (4 pages, dont la page de garde) ; aucune figure ni schéma dans le sujet, donc aucune image produite. Page de garde vérifiée : ORDINARY LEVEL, 0540 FOOD AND NUTRITION 1, JUNE 2025, QCM d'une heure et demie. Le sujet n'imprime pas la mention de la calculatrice non programmable.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les 50 clés sont déduites du programme O Level Food and Nutrition. Le sujet imprime des fautes (Odema, phosphorous, Mauses, Hons d'oeuvre, Jellof, labeled, « greatly link ») recopiées telles quelles ; la question 17 écrit B12 avec un indice, rendu en LaTeX.
Aucun calcul numérique dans le sujet, sauf la question 50 (16 cuillères à soupe pour une tasse de mesure : 240 ml / 15 ml = 16 ; 250 ml / 15 ml = 16,67), recalculée avec Python.
Question 50 : aucune des options imprimées (4, 8, 6, 2) n'est exacte (une tasse standard = environ 16 cuillères à soupe) ; aucune lettre choisie, question ouverte.

Question 11 : l'énoncé imprimé est inversé (la vitamine D aide à l'absorption du calcium et du phosphore, et non l'inverse) ; la vitamine D (B) est la seule option liée au calcium et au phosphore. Question 47 : « contains antibodies » (C) et « is nutritionally balanced » (D) sont toutes deux défendables ; réponse visée D. Ces deux questions sont ouvertes.

Clés raisonnées mais discutables, à relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition : 1 (molecules), 7 (young people ; old women est défendable pour la prévention de l'ostéoporose), 21 (salmon, poisson anadrome classé avec les poissons d'eau douce ; cod, herring et mackerel sont marins), 22 (how long the food can last ; D « kept in a shop » est trop étroit), 25 (erepsin, ancien nom des peptidases intestinales), 28 (fish pastries ; « Mauses » est probablement une mousse), 32 (pasteurization and bottling ; dehydration n'est pas une méthode par la chaleur), 34 (griddle and spit roaster), 39 (15 à 52 °C contient la température du corps ; les trois autres plages sont étroites et froides), 41 (puree ; pottage est aussi un potage épais), 45 (oval ; crescent est défendable), 48 (covering with a gauze, pression sur la plaie ; tying with a bandage est défendable).

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 11, 47. Question 11 : énoncé inversé, réponse visée B (vitamin D). Question 47 : options C et D défendables, réponse visée D. Question 50 : voir l'entrée précédente (aucune option exacte, conversion faite à la rédaction).

questions.enonce_markdown: The chemical elements that make up food are arranged in the form of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Food is made of nutrients such as carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins and water. These are chemical substances, that is, molecules built by joining chemical elements (carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen and so on) together in definite arrangements. Cells make up living things, not the chemical structure of a food. "Elements" repeats the question instead of naming an arrangement of them, and amino acids are only the building blocks of proteins, not of all food.

**Answer: A.**
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Bad breath is also described as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Halitosis is the medical name for bad breath. It is often caused by food particles left between the teeth, poor mouth hygiene or gum disease. Periodontal disease and gingivitis are diseases of the gums and tissues around the teeth (bad breath can be a sign of them, but it is not their name), and dental caries is tooth decay.

**Answer: B.**
themes: dental health and diet in nutrition

questions.enonce_markdown: An inadequate supply of protein and energy food is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question names a lack of both protein and energy foods. That condition is called protein energy malnutrition (PEM). Kwashiorkor is the form of PEM in which protein is especially lacking, and marasmus is the form in which the whole food intake (energy and protein) is very low, so each of them is only one type of PEM. Energy deficiency mentions energy only.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following groups of food is rich in first class protein?
questions.corrige_markdown:
First class (complete) proteins contain all the essential amino acids in the right proportions. They come mainly from animal foods: meat, fish, eggs, milk and cheese. Option C is the only group made entirely of animal foods (fish, cheese and milk). Groundnuts, nuts and mushrooms are plant foods whose proteins are second class (incomplete), so options A, B and D each contain a trap.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Sucrose is found mostly in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sucrose is a sugar (disaccharide) found in sugar cane, sugar beet and in sweet fruits such as pineapple, mango and orange. Cereals and pulses store their carbohydrate mainly as starch, and nuts are rich in fat and protein, so fruits are the best answer.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Saturated fatty acids are greatly link to one of the following:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A diet rich in saturated fats (animal fats, butter, palm oil, fried and fatty foods) supplies a lot of energy, so it favours weight gain and obesity, and it also raises the risk of heart disease. Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of protein, oedema (printed "Odema") is swelling that can be a sign of kwashiorkor, and rickets is caused by lack of vitamin D or calcium.

**Answer: C.**
themes: fats and oils in the diet

questions.enonce_markdown: More calcium intake is needed by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Calcium builds bones and teeth, so the need is greatest during growth, in children, adolescents and young people, and also in pregnant and breast-feeding women. Overweight people do not need extra calcium because of their weight. Old people need to keep an adequate intake to slow bone loss, but the group that needs more calcium because their bodies are still building bone is young people.

**Answer: C.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: \_\_\_\_\_\_ will assist in blood clotting.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Calcium is needed, together with vitamin K, for the blood to clot at a cut. Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, iodine is needed to make thyroxine (it prevents goitre), and potassium helps nerve and muscle action and the water balance of the body.

**Answer: B.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: A substance that prevents food from separation during processing is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An emulsifier (for example lecithin) holds together two substances that do not normally mix, such as oil and water, so the food does not separate into layers (as in mayonnaise or margarine). An antioxidant stops fats from going rancid, and a preservative slows spoilage by micro-organisms. "Food additive" is the general name for all of these substances, not the one that stops separation.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Peas, beans and lentils belong to a family known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Peas, beans and lentils are seeds that grow in pods. They belong to the legume (pulse) family. They are rich in protein, but "proteins" is a nutrient, not the name of a plant family. Nuts have a hard shell and are rich in fat, and "vegetables" is a much wider group.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calcium and phosphorous are highly needed for the proper functioning of:

*Options as printed:* A) Vitamin C   B) Vitamin D   C) Iron   D) Vitamin A
questions.corrige_markdown:
Calcium and phosphorus are the minerals that build bones and teeth, and vitamin D is the vitamin that helps the body to absorb them and put them into the bones. Of the four options, vitamin D is therefore the one linked to calcium and phosphorus. The printed sentence is however reversed (vitamin D is needed for the proper use of calcium and phosphorus, not the other way round), so the question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically.

**Intended answer: B (Vitamin D).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: A document that give ingredients and instruction for preparing a specific food is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A recipe lists the ingredients, their quantities and the method for preparing a particular dish. A food composition table lists the nutrients in foods, a dietary guideline is advice on healthy eating, and a food label gives information about a packaged food (ingredients and nutrition information) but no preparation instructions.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Fats will emulsify during digestion in the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fats are emulsified (broken into tiny droplets) by bile, which is made in the liver, stored in the gall bladder and poured into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. Emulsification gives the enzyme lipase a bigger surface to work on. No bile is added in the mouth or the stomach, and the ileum is mainly where digested food is absorbed.

**Answer: D.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown: Bacteria may be destroyed during digestion by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The stomach produces hydrochloric acid, which makes the stomach contents very acidic and kills most of the bacteria swallowed with food. Saliva, intestinal juice and bile are there mainly to help digest food, so the acid of the stomach is the main protection.

**Answer: D.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown: The vitamin required for proper formation of bones and teeth is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cholecalciferol is vitamin D (vitamin D3). It helps the body absorb calcium and phosphorus so that bones and teeth are properly formed, and its lack causes rickets in children. Tocopherol is vitamin E, retinol is vitamin A (vision, skin) and riboflavin is vitamin B2.

**Answer: B.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Another name given to loss of memory is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Dementia is a condition, most common in old age, in which memory and thinking are progressively lost. Dermatitis is inflammation of the skin, and periodontal (disease) and plaque are problems of the gums and teeth.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the chemical name for vitamin B$_{12}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vitamin B$_{12}$ is called cobalamin, because it contains the mineral cobalt. It is found in animal foods and its lack causes pernicious anaemia. Thiamin is vitamin B$_1$, riboflavin is vitamin B$_2$ and niacin is vitamin B$_3$.

**Answer: A.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following lubricates joints and membranes?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Water is the main part of the fluids that lubricate the joints (synovial fluid) and keep the membranes moist. Water also carries nutrients and wastes, and helps to control body temperature. Vitamins, minerals and proteins do not act as lubricants.

**Answer: D.**
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the energy that helps in the transmission of nervous impulse.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A nerve impulse is a small electrical signal that travels along the nerve cell, so the energy involved in transmitting it is electrical energy. The food we eat supplies chemical energy, and heat and mechanical energy are given out by the body in other ways (body warmth, muscle movement).

**Answer: A.**
themes: energy from food and body metabolism

questions.enonce_markdown: The main component of tendon is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tendons join muscles to bones and are made mainly of collagen, a strong protein in the form of fibres. In meat cookery this is the tough connective tissue that is changed into gelatine by slow, moist cooking. "Fibres" is too general, since muscle also has fibres, and tendons are not made of muscle or lipids.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of fresh water fish is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cod, herring and mackerel are sea (salt water) fish. Salmon is the fish of the list that is classed with the fresh water fish (it is born and grows in rivers and lakes, and returns there to breed), so B is the best answer.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The 'shelf-life' of food is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Shelf-life is the length of time a food can be stored and still be safe and of good quality. It is about how long the food lasts, wherever it is kept, so option D, which limits it to a shop, is too narrow. It concerns the food itself and not only its taste or its nutrients.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: How long the food can last
How long the nutrients can last
How long the food can be kept in a shop

questions.enonce_markdown: Food is being labeled to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A food label tells the buyer what the product is, its ingredients, weight, date of manufacture or expiry ("best before") date and storage instructions, so that customers can choose and use it safely. Labelling does not keep the taste, prevent contamination or preserve the flavour: that is the job of the packaging and of preservation.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Appetite and the desire to eat food is affected by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Appetite is the desire to eat. It is stimulated by the sight, smell, taste and texture (feel in the mouth) of food, which make the mouth water. Availability of food, climate, time and facilities influence what people eat (food habits), but it is the senses that directly affect appetite.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the enzyme that completes protein digestion.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Pepsin (stomach) and trypsin (pancreas) break proteins into shorter chains (peptides). Erepsin, the enzyme of the intestinal juice (now called peptidases), finishes the job by splitting peptides into amino acids, which can be absorbed. Trypsinogen is only the inactive form of trypsin, and rennin curdles milk in the stomach of babies.

**Answer: B.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown: Modern kitchens usually have drainage system for:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A modern kitchen has a sink with drains and pipes that carry the waste water (dirty water from washing food and dishes) out of the house. Its purpose is not to remove clean running water, and standing and stagnant water are only waste water left to stay in one place.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: \_\_\_\_\_\_ is stored in the liver as reserved energy.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Extra glucose from digested carbohydrates is changed into glycogen (animal starch) and stored in the liver and the muscles. When the body needs energy, glycogen is changed back into glucose. Glucose circulates in the blood, and sucrose and lactose are sugars found in foods.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: \_\_\_\_\_\_ is an example of a savory dish.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A savory dish has a salty or spicy taste and is usually served as a starter or a side dish, not as a sweet dish. Fish pastries (for example fish pie or fish rolls) are savory. Fruit juice and fruit salad are sweet, and the first option (printed "Mauses", probably a misspelling of mousse) is normally a sweet dish when it is not specified otherwise.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A three course meal consist of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A three course meal is one meal served in three parts: a starter (appetizer), a main course (main meal) and a dessert. Breakfast, lunch and dinner are three different meals of the day and not three courses of one meal.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A meal that starts with the main dish and ends with dessert is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A two course meal has only two parts: the main dish followed by a dessert. Hors d'oeuvre (printed "Hons d'oeuvre") is a small starter, which this meal does not have, and "savory meal" and "second course meal" are not names of a meal pattern.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Plunging vegetable rapidly in boiling water and rapidly cooling is described as
questions.corrige_markdown:
Blanching means putting vegetables in boiling water for a very short time and then cooling them quickly in cold water. It is used before freezing, to keep the colour, and to remove the skin of fruits such as tomatoes. Pickling is preserving in vinegar, boiling is cooking for a longer time, and steaming cooks in the steam without putting the food in the water.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the followings are heat preservative methods?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Heat preservation kills or slows the micro-organisms that spoil food by heating it. Pasteurization (for example of milk) and bottling (heating food in sealed jars) both use heat. In the other options, dehydration is drying (removing water) and irradiation uses rays, while oxidation is not a method of preservation at all (it spoils fats). Sterilization is a heat method, but in B and C it is paired with a method that is not.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Pick out a separate base unit.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An island unit is a base unit that stands on its own in the middle of the kitchen floor, separate from the walls and from the other units, with space to walk all around it. A peninsular unit is joined at one end to a wall or to other units, wall units are fixed on the wall above the worktop, and tall units stand on the floor against the wall.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cookers also have some additional features like:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Besides the basic parts of a cooker (hob, oven, grill and control knobs), some cookers have extra features such as a griddle, a spit roaster, an automatic timer or a plate warmer. Option B names two real extras. The hob, the oven and the knobs are basic parts of a cooker, not additional ones, which rules out A, C and D.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The warmest part of the cabinet of a refrigerator is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Every time the door is opened, warm air from the room enters, and the shelves on the door are the closest to it and the least cooled, so they are the warmest part of the refrigerator. They are used for foods that keep well, such as bottled drinks, sauces and butter.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One way of heat transfer in a microwave oven is by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A microwave oven cooks by radiation: microwaves (a type of electromagnetic wave) enter the food and make its water molecules vibrate, which heats the food. Conduction and convection are how heat then spreads inside the food, but the way the energy reaches the food is radiation. Irradiation is a method of food preservation with rays, not a way of transferring heat in cooking.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cooking method whereby water does not come in direct contact with food is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In steaming, the food is cooked by the steam rising from boiling water, usually in a steamer or a covered dish placed over the water, so the water does not touch the food. Braising, stewing and boiling are all done with the food in contact with some liquid.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Experiencing double vision after eating food could be a symptom of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Double vision is a typical sign of botulism, the food poisoning caused by the toxin of Clostridium botulinum, which grows in badly canned or bottled food. The toxin attacks the nerves and also causes blurred vision, difficulty in swallowing and muscle weakness. Salmonella and Staphylococcus aureus cause mainly vomiting, diarrhoea and stomach pain. Option B ("Clostridium bacteria") is too general, because other Clostridium bacteria cause different illnesses.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Bacteria will grow rapidly under temperature ranges from:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bacteria multiply fastest in warm conditions, at the temperature of the human body (about 37°C) and around it. Only option A contains this temperature (15°C to 52°C). The three other ranges are narrow and cool, a zone where growth is slow, close to refrigerator temperature.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cake that has risen and cracked on the top indicates a fault arising from:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When the oven is too hot, the outside of the cake sets and forms a crust before the middle has finished rising. The centre then goes on rising, pushes through the crust and cracks it. Too much sugar, too much liquid or too much water give other faults (a flat, sunken, heavy or sticky cake).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Soups made from pulse vegetables and other types of vegetables are known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Puree soups are made from pulses (peas, beans, lentils) and other vegetables cooked until soft and then sieved or blended into a thick smooth soup. A broth is a thin soup made from meat, fish or vegetable stock, and gravy is a sauce made from the juices of cooked meat. Pottage is a thick soup too, but the name for a soup of sieved vegetables is puree.

**Answer: B.**
themes: soup making and types of soup

questions.enonce_markdown: Two foods necessary for cocktail parties are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
At a cocktail party guests stand, hold a drink and eat small "finger foods" with their fingers, such as small biscuits, canapes, small pastries and scotch eggs. Butter biscuits and scotch eggs fit this. Jellof rice, dodo (fried plantain) and fried egg are normal meal dishes that need a plate and cutlery, and scones are usually served at tea.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Formal invitations are used for which ceremonies?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A formal invitation (a printed card with the host, the occasion, date, time and place) is used for important ceremonies such as weddings and ordinations. Birthday parties and religious crusades are usually announced informally (by word of mouth, a call, a message or a poster).

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Religious crusades and installation of leaders

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following services are suitable for a sick person in bed?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tray service is used when a person cannot come to the table: the whole meal is arranged on a tray (with a tray cloth, plate, cutlery, napkin and drink) and brought to the bed. Kitchen, buffet and formal service are for people who sit or stand in the dining area.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The best flower arrangement for a dining table is?
questions.corrige_markdown:
On a dining table the flowers must be low and compact, so that guests can see and talk to each other across the table, and they must look good from all sides. A round or oval arrangement does this. A vertical or triangular arrangement is tall and blocks the view, and a crescent arrangement is shaped to be seen from one side (for a sideboard or a mantelpiece).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following kitchen equipment is used for straining vegetables and pasta?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A colander is a large bowl with holes in it, used to drain the water from boiled vegetables and pasta. A sieve and a strainer have a fine mesh and are used for small quantities of liquids and fine foods (flour, tea, sauces). A vegetable basket is for storing vegetables.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Breast milk is nutritionally important to babies because it:

*Options as printed:* A) Has the right temperature   B) Is cheap   C) Contains antibodies   D) Is nutritionally balanced
questions.corrige_markdown:
Breast milk contains protein, fat, lactose sugar, vitamins and minerals in the right proportions for a baby, so it is nutritionally balanced, and this is what makes it nutritionally important. It also contains antibodies that protect the baby against infections, which is a protective value rather than a nutritional one. The right temperature and the low cost are advantages but not nutritional ones. Because options C and D can both be defended, the question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically.

**Intended answer: D (Is nutritionally balanced).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Blood flow from a cut in the finger can be stopped by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
To stop bleeding from a small cut, press on it with a clean pad of gauze (or clean cloth) and keep the finger raised until the bleeding stops. Washing with water or putting iodine cleans the wound or kills germs but does not stop the blood flow, and a bandage tied tightly can stop the blood supply to the finger, so a pad of gauze is the best answer.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Milk is called a perfect food because it:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Milk is called a perfect (complete) food because it contains all the main nutrients: protein, fat, carbohydrate (lactose), vitamins, minerals and water. Option C lists only two of them, and being a creamy liquid or being easily digested does not make a food complete. (Milk is however low in iron and in vitamin C, so it is not perfect for an adult as the only food.)

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Contains all the essential food nutrient

questions.enonce_markdown:
How many table spoons will make up a standard measuring cup?

*Options as printed:* A) 4   B) 8   C) 6   D) 2
questions.corrige_markdown:
A standard measuring cup holds 16 level tablespoons (about 240 ml, with 1 tablespoon about 15 ml). With a cup of 250 ml the result is about 16.7, so in all cases it is about 16 tablespoons. None of the four printed options (4, 8, 6 and 2) is correct: 8 tablespoons make half a cup.

**Intended answer: none of the printed options (the correct value is about 16 tablespoons).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
